articles.title: Bengaluru Suburban Rail project moves ahead, but just 19.9% work done in 3.5 years
articles.description: BSTP has recorded 19.9% physical progress as of July, while K-RIDE pushes fresh tenders, land acquisition and level-crossing removal. The project will also shift to ETCS Level-2 and feature a 1.2-km double-decker stretch at Mathikere. Bengaluru’s long-awaited suburban rail project is moving forward with several key works, but its overall physical progress remains at 19.9% after three-and-a-half years. The latest progress update was provided by Rail Infrastructure Development Company (Karnataka) Limited (K-RIDE) in its July project newsletter. K-RIDE Managing Director Lakshman Singh said tenders have now been invited for around 9 km of viaduct works on Corridor-2. The agency has also started the tender process for two major packages covering 22 km on Corridor-4. Corridor-4, which will connect Heelalige and Rajanakunte, stretches for 46.8 km. One of the major tasks planned on this corridor is the removal of all 11 level crossings along the existing railway line. The tender process for this work has already begun. Also Read: Bengaluru gets 1.2-km double-decker transport structure at Mathikere: Road below, suburban rail above Work is also progressing on the proposed Akkupete depot. The state government has issued an order allowing execution of the depot works, while the process of acquiring private land needed for the depot approach has already started. One of the major changes in the project is the signalling and train-control technology. BSTP w as initially planned to use Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC), similar to the system planned for Namma Metro’s Pink and Blue Lines. K-RIDE has now confirmed that this plan has been changed. The suburban rail network will instead use the European Train Control System (ETCS) Level-2 across all BSTP corridors. The same technology is proposed for India’s first high-speed rail project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. ETCS Level-2 is expected to improve railway safety by providing real-time information and monitoring train movements. The system is part of K-RIDE’s broader effort to create a safer and more efficient suburban rail network. Also Read: Bengaluru metro Yellow Line may extend to Attibele, near Tamil Nadu border K-RIDE has also highlighted the project’s focus on reducing the need for additional land acquisition and controlling costs. According to the agency, the planned solutions are intended to reduce traffic congestion, improve mobility, address water stagnation problems and provide safer connectivity across Bengaluru. Another important engineering feature is coming up on Mohan Kumar Road between Mathikere and Yeshwantpur. A 1.2-km double-decker structure will be built in this congested urban stretch. Instead of creating separate structures for road and rail, both will be accommodated within the same corridor. The first level will function as a road flyover, allowing vehicles to move through the area. The second level will carry the elevated suburban rail viaduct of Corridor-2. The arrangement is aimed at making better use of the limited space available in the densely developed Mathikere-Yeshwantpur area. By placing the road and railway infrastructure one above the other, K-RIDE expects to optimise the available urban space while limiting the requirement for additional land. Also Read: Independence Day weekend: KIA warns passengers of possible delays, here’s what travellers should know The developments are significant for Corridor-2, which runs between Benniganahalli and Chikkabanavara, and Corridor-4, which will connect Heelalige to Rajanakunte. With fresh tenders, depot work, land acquisition, level-crossing elimination and the adoption of ETCS Level-2, several components of the Bengaluru Suburban Transport Project are now moving into important execution stages. However, the overall project has so far achieved only 19.9% physical progress as of July, highlighting the distance still left before Bengaluru gets its full suburban rail network.

articles.title: G.S. Patil, Salim Ahmed file nominations for Presiding Officer posts in Karnataka Legislature
articles.description: Bengaluru, Aug 13 (IANS) Congress MLA G.S. Patil on Thursday filed his nomination for the post of Karnataka Legislative Assembly Speaker in the presence of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. Patil submitted his nomination papers at the office of Assembly Secretary Vishalakshi in the Vidhana Soudha. Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, Minister K.H. Muniyappa, KPCC president and MLC B.K. Hariprasad, and former Minister H.K. Patil were present on the occasion. Meanwhile, Congress MLC Salim Ahmed filed his nomination for the post of Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council. The election to the post is scheduled to be held on Friday. Ahmed submitted his nomination papers at the office of the Legislative Council Secretary in the presence of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah, KPCC president and MLC B.K. Hariprasad, Vinay Karthik and Nagaraj Yadav were among those present when Ahmed filed his nomination. Meanwhile, the BJP MLCs held a meeting under the leadership of the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy and discussed about the development and election to the post of the Chairman of the Legislative Council. It can be noted that former Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti had said he had to sign his resignation letter under compulsion, alleging that he was not given the opportunity to resign on the day he had planned. Horatti said he had conveyed all details regarding his resignation to the Governor, but had not received any communication confirming whether his resignation had been accepted. “I have conveyed everything to the Governor in this regard. The Governor has not given me any intimation. He has not stated whether I have been relieved or whether my resignation has been accepted. As far as I know, if I have been appointed as the pro tem Chairman, it means my resignation has been accepted,” Horatti said. Horatti expressed disappointment over the state government’s handling of the issue and said he was hurt by the developments. “I am pained by the move of the state government. I have not done anything wrong. I am saddened. I have been in the House for 46 years and have rendered my services. I had to resign under a compulsive situation. I did not want a confrontational situation,” he said. Horatti said he had discussed the timing of his resignation with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and that there had been an understanding between them on the matter. “What I had discussed with the Chief Minister was that on August 13, we would complete the obituary references and on August 14, the Vice Chairman would be elected. I had said that on that day, I would get an opportunity to convey my gratitude. I had told him that after expressing my gratitude on that day, I would tender my resignation. I had also made an announcement to this effect,” he said. --IANS mka/rad
